interventions.name: Agroforestry Intercropping with Nitrogen-Fixing Legumes
interventions.ecological_mechanism: Incorporating nitrogen-fixing leguminous trees (e.g., Acacia, Gliricidia) and cover crops into monoculture cereals enhances atmospheric nitrogen fixation (rhizobial symbioses), increases litter turnover, improves soil organic matter pool, shades soil to lower microclimate evapotranspiration, and restores mycorrhizal fungi networks.
sources: FAO (2020) State of the World's Forests: Forests, Biodiversity and People
IPCC (2019) Special Report on Climate Change and Land (SRCCL), Chapter 4: Land Degradation
Jose, S. (2009) Agroforestry for ecosystem services. Agroforestry Systems, 76(1), 1-10.

interventions.name: Biochar Soil Amendment with Micro-Dose Organic Compost
interventions.ecological_mechanism: Pyrolyzed biomass (biochar) creates a highly porous recalcitrant carbon skeleton that buffers acidic soil pH, boosts cation exchange capacity (CEC), sequesters persistent recalcitrant carbon for decades, and retains soil moisture during dry spells, preventing nutrient leaching.
sources: IPCC (2022) AR6 Working Group III: Mitigation of Climate Change, Chapter 12: CDR Technologies
Lehmann, J. et al. (2015) Biochar for Environmental Management: Science, Technology and Implementation.

interventions.name: Biodiverse Hedgerow Buffers & Riparian Conservation Corridors
interventions.ecological_mechanism: Establishing multi-layered native woody hedgerows and riparian vegetated buffer strips traps agricultural chemical runoff before entering aquatic ecosystems, breaks up large monoculture patches into connected ecological corridors, provides nesting micro-habitats for native bees and predatory insects (natural biological control agents), and mitigates edge effects.
sources: IPBES (2019) Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
FAO & ITPS (2020) State of Knowledge of Soil Biodiversity: Status, Challenges and Potential
Benton, T. G. et al. (2003) Farmland biodiversity: is habitat heterogeneity the key? Trends in Ecology & Evolution.

interventions.name: Regenerative Conservation Tillage & Multispecies Cover Cropping
interventions.ecological_mechanism: Transitioning from heavy inversion plowing to zero-till or strip-till combined with 8-12 species cover crop cocktails prevents soil crusting, creates biopores through deep taproots, insulates soil skin against solar radiation, stimulates earthworm (Lumbricidae) populations, and drastically reduces carbon oxidation.
sources: FAO (2021) Soil Organic Carbon Mapping & Conservation Agriculture Technical Guide
Lal, R. (2004) Soil carbon sequestration impacts on global climate change and food security. Science, 304(5677), 1623-1627.
